In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in our studies, the carcinogenicity of N-nitrosonornicotine (NNN), nitrosodiphenylamine (DPA), and NM was not significantly inhibited by NaASC.
NaASC, gallic acid and thiocyanate inhibit lung adenoma induction by amines plus NaNO2, but not by nitrosamines.
NaASC, gallic acid or caffeine can be used in the prevention of nitrosamine carcinogenesis, but that the use of thiocyanate should be abandoned.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the carcinogenicity of N-nitro compounds can be greatly increased or decreased, depending on whether or not the nitrosation is followed by nitrosation of a second amine, which can be a drug or a metabolite of the drug.
the carcinogenic action of N-nitro-samines is not inhibited by gallic and caffeic acids, but is strongly inhibited by ascorbate and thiocyanate.
the effects of NaASC, thiocyanates, gallic acid and caffeine on the induction of lung adenomas by nitrosamines or nitrosamides plus nitrite were complex, but that NaASC was an effective inhibitor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the carcinogenic potential of a drug is not known, a carcinogenicity bioassay should be performed.
, in the presence of nitrite, the carcinogenicity of amines or amines plus nitrite can be greatly reduced by the addition of ascorbate.
it should be possible to prevent the induction of lung adenomas in mice by nitrosatable drugs and NaNO2 in the diet.
